prerequisites: Linear Algebra, Analytical and Differential Geometry (year 1)

learning_outcomes.text: Defines basic notions from the studied special mathematics chapters.
Understands the mathematical objects described in the course.
Acquires theoretical concepts and develops skills to work with them.
Forms logical mental attitudes for problem-solving.
Explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results in mathematics.
Applies calculation formulas, theorems, and criteria studied in the special mathematics chapters to complex problems.
Operates with basic concepts, principles, and methods from the studied special mathematics chapters.
Solves mathematical problems with applicability in engineering and validates the obtained solution.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the workgroup and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents themselves in their field of activity by adequately using effective learning methods and techniques throughout life.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 1 Systems of Differential Equations
1.1. General definitions. Normal form of a system of differential equations
1.2. Geometric and mechanical interpretation of solutions of a system of differential equations. Phase space
1.3. Symmetric systems
1.4. Systems of first-order linear differential equations
1.5. Systems of linear differential equations with constant coefficients
1.6. Multiple roots of the characteristic equation
1.7. Matrix form of a system of linear differential equations
1.8. Equivalence of a system of linear differential equations with an n-order linear differential equation. Ordinary, linear, homogeneous and non-homogeneous differential equations of order n.
Chapter 2 First-order linear and quasi-linear partial differential equations
2.1. First-order linear partial differential equations: definitions; integral surfaces
2.2. Characteristic system. Characteristic curves
2.3. General solution
2.4. Cauchy's problem
2.5. First-order quasi-linear partial differential equations
2.6. General solution
2.7. Cauchy's problem.
Chapter 3 Elements of Field Theory
3.1. Scalar fields. Level surfaces. Level curves
3.2. Derivative along a direction of a scalar field. Gradient of a scalar field
3.3. Vector fields. Field lines and field surfaces of a vector field
3.4. Review of integrals in scalar and vector fields: curvilinear integrals; surface integrals; triple integrals
3.5. Gauss-Ostrogradski formula
3.6. Potential field
3.7. Divergence and curl of a vector field
3.8. Hamilton operator and its repeated application
3.9. Integral formulas.
Chapter 4 Complex Functions of a Complex Variable
4.1. Complex numbers. Geometric interpretation
4.2. Functions of a complex variable
4.3. Derivative of a complex function of a complex variable: Cauchy-Riemann conditions; analytic function
4.4. Elementary complex functions.
Chapter 5 Integration in the Complex Plane
5.1. Curvilinear integral in the complex plane. Properties
5.2. Cauchy's theorems
5.3. Indefinite integral
5.4. Cauchy integral
5.5. Integrals in complex depending on a parameter
5.6. Expression of derivatives of various orders of a holomorphic function.
Chapter 6 Series of Analytic Functions
6.1. Uniformly convergent series of analytic functions
6.2. Power series in complex. Abel's Theorem
6.3. Taylor series in complex
6.4. Laurent series and isolated points of a complex function
6.5. Expansion of an analytic function into a Laurent series
6.6. Classification of singular points.
Chapter 7 Residue Theory and its Applications
7.1. Residue of an analytic function at an isolated singular point
7.2. Formulas for calculating residues
7.3. Residue theorem
7.4. Calculation of real integrals using the residue theorem.
Chapter 8 Fourier Series
8.1. Trigonometric series
8.2. Fourier series of a periodic function
8.3. Fourier series of an even function and an odd function
8.4. Complex form of a Fourier series
Chapter 9 Fourier Integral and Fourier Transforms
9.1. Complex form of a Fourier integral
9.2. Real form of the Fourier integral
9.3. Fourier integrals of an even or odd function
9.4. Fourier Transform
9.5. Properties of the Fourier Transform.
Seminar: Systems of differential equations
Seminar: First-order linear and quasi-linear partial differential equations
Seminar: Elements of field theory
Seminar: Complex functions of a complex variable
Seminar: Integration in the complex plane
Seminar: Series of analytic functions
Seminar: Residue theory and its applications
Seminar: Fourier series
Seminar: Fourier integral and Fourier transforms
teaching_methods: Debates based on theoretical notions presented on the blackboard by the professor
Recapitulation of notions from the previous course
Discovery-based learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality (demonstration, modeling)
Exposition with electronic whiteboard associated with an integrated e-learning system
Practical applications to topics discussed in class
Exercises and problems worked on the blackboard

assessment_methods.method: Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Integer grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with a grade of 5 certifying the achievement of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of its associated study credits.
